critique: The draft is faithful, keeps the structure, links and frontmatter intact, and has no dashes, gender problems or accuracy claims. Its weaknesses are a handful of English calques that read as translated: "nenhuma quantidade de mexidas", "através da qual discordar", "dentro de 8 graus do exato" and "difícil de passar despercebida". A few word choices are also stiff ("gatilho sensível" for hair trigger, "começa incêndios") and there is a clumsy repetition in the final sentence.

The draft is faithful, gender-neutral toward the reader and free of dashes, and the frontmatter is in order. The main problems are a few unidiomatic or slightly inaccurate phrases. "Vivida pelos outros" in the description misstates "lived out through other people," and "senta o que você está construindo" is an odd transitive use. There are also several calques: "dividir a diferença," "deixa com fome" and "com outro elenco." The sentence about the people who irritate or fascinate you is clunky and repeats "interpretar."

The draft is clean and faithful. Terminology (sextil, trígono, quadratura, orbe, mapa astral), Brazilian spelling, the você register, links, frontmatter enums and length limits are all correct, and there are no dashes and no gendered address to the reader. The only fix is one slightly clumsy construction in the second section.

The draft is accurate and faithful, with clean frontmatter, intact links and no dashes. Its problems are a few calques of English: the abrupt "É quadratura.", the headings "Como uma quadratura se sente" and "Trabalhando uma quadratura", "empurram com o dobro da força" and "leva a briga para debaixo da terra". Gender handling for the reader is already neutral.

The draft is faithful and mostly natural, with no dashes, no link problems and no gendered address to the reader. The main fixes are a gender inconsistency on "orbe", which is masculine in Brazilian astrology usage, and a missing subjunctive. Two phrasings read as calques of the English and were reworked. The theme line added "em troca", which the English does not say, so it was removed.

The draft is accurate and keeps the English structure, links and frontmatter, but the description runs past 155 characters and needs trimming. It uses "partilhado" throughout, which reads as European Portuguese; Brazilian readers expect "compartilhado". One FAQ answer addresses the reader in the masculine ("sozinho"), which needs a neutral rephrase.

The draft is accurate, keeps the structure, links and frontmatter intact, and contains no dashes or gendered address to the reader. The problems are a few spots of awkward grammar or calqued idiom. In the FAQ, "em que você já está encaminhado" uses the wrong preposition. "Criou você pela metade" and "amigos que sustentam a estrutura" read as literal translations of English idioms, and "nenhum deles é mais sociável que o outro" mismatches the comparison across four signs.

The draft is faithful, clean of dashes, and its links and frontmatter follow the rules. The remaining problems are a few literal or ambiguous phrasings in the planets section. "Graça" is ambiguous for "fun." "Estado de repouso" and "se ilumina" are calques of "resting state" and "lifts." "Chega com cuidado" reads oddly. The rest reads as natural Brazilian Portuguese.

The draft is accurate, well registered and free of dashes, gender assumptions and invented claims. Its main problems are a few English calques ("não concordam", "no meio da passada", "passar dele") and a loose rendering of "rising sign" as plain "ascendente" in two places. The plain version makes one FAQ question and one sentence in the body circular, since the article defines the ascendente as the degree and then calls the sign "o seu ascendente". Frontmatter, links and structure are correct.

The draft is accurate and reads naturally, with correct Brazilian terminology (Fundo do Céu, Meio do Céu, casa 4, cúspide, signos inteiros). It has no dashes and no gendered address to the reader. The flagged description was 156 characters and needed trimming. Two calqued constructions also needed smoothing: the elliptical "e há cerca de dois mil anos" and "discutem ... há quase toda a história registrada."

The draft is accurate, keeps the structure and links intact, and has no dashes or added claims. Most problems are idiom calques. The draft is accurate, faithful to the English structure, and largely natural, with consistent Brazilian terminology and correctly localized links. One phrase about Jupiter ("no caminho de volta de recebê-los") was a clumsy calque and has been smoothed. Frontmatter, lengths, and dashes are clean.

The draft is clean overall: it is faithful to the source, keeps the structure, frontmatter and links correct, uses the Brazilian terms (casa 7, ascendente, descendente, cúspide, signos inteiros) consistently and contains no dashes. The remaining problems are a few English calques ("na altura dos olhos", "Essa oposição é o ponto"), one ungrammatical relative clause ("que é para isso que serve"), and an ambiguous pronoun that could be read as referring to Saturno. I fixed only these and left the rest as drafted.

The draft is faithful, with correct links, structure and frontmatter, and contains no dashes. The draft is accurate, faithful and mostly natural Brazilian Portuguese, with correct links, terminology and frontmatter. The flagged description was over 155 characters and has been shortened. Three phrases were fixed: a missing preposition in a relative clause, the calque "de acordo" for "accordingly", and the calque "forma de arte nativa", which could also be confused with the astrological "nativo".

The draft is accurate, well structured and keeps every link and frontmatter value correctly. The draft is accurate, keeps the structure and links, and has no dashes. The draft is accurate and keeps the English structure, frontmatter and links. The opening line and the FAQ line about luck were also awkward. One phrase assigned a gender to a generic "quem" without need, and a few word choices ("senso de tempo", "contada à altura") are not what a Brazilian writer would use.

The draft is accurate, keeps the structure and links intact, and has no dashes or frontmatter problems. The fixes are minor. "a viagem sozinho" assigns a gender to the traveler. "está segurando" lacks an object. "o casamento que ampliou o mapa" can be misread as the birth chart in this context. A few phrasings read as calques ("ficar bem", "encontrar crescimento"). The draft is faithful and mostly natural, and its frontmatter, links and dash usage are clean. The description's "a generosidade que não conta" reads as "generosity that doesn't matter", so it needed rewording within the 155-character limit. A few spots read as calques or colloquial slips: "uma sala" for reading a room, "o benefício de toda dúvida", "chamar... de a mais produtiva" and "sem virar ela". The body also had a comma-spliced parenthetical, an awkward "lugar onde não sentir tudo", and "se perde" where the English means waste.

The draft is faithful in structure, facts, links and frontmatter, and has no dashes or gendered address to the reader. These are smoothed into natural idiom, and everything else is left as it was.

The draft is accurate, keeps the structure and links intact, and contains no dashes or added claims. The draft is accurate, faithful in structure and facts, free of dashes, and uses standard Brazilian terminology and correct links. The remaining problems are a few English calques. "Domínio de pavio longo" reads oddly because "pavio curto" means short-tempered in Portuguese. "Baste como cadeiras" is an unnatural rendering of "be enough chairs." "Parecia com frio" can be misread as "resembled cold."

The draft is accurate, natural Brazilian Portuguese with consistent terminology, correct agreement and no dashes. The main problem is that the description runs about 173 characters, over the 155 limit. One small calque ("isso se lê como") reads stiffly and was smoothed. Links, enum fields and dates follow the rules.

The draft is faithful and mostly reads as natural Brazilian Portuguese, with correct terminology, links and frontmatter. The draft is accurate, keeps the structure and links intact, and has no dashes or added claims. The draft is accurate and natural, and the links and frontmatter follow the rules. The description exceeded 155 characters, so I shortened it. The draft is accurate, faithful and free of dashes. Frontmatter, links and FAQ order are correct, and the description is exactly 155 characters. The draft is accurate and mostly natural, with correct frontmatter, links and terminology and no dashes. The draft is accurate, keeps the structure, and has no dashes or link problems. The draft is accurate, keeps every link and the full structure, and contains no dashes.
